source.title: On the Interpretability of Regularisation for Neural Networks Through Model Gradient Similarity
source.authors: Vincent Szolnoky; Viktor Andersson; B. Kulcsár; Rebecka Jörnsten

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies randomly flipped training labels and reports test accuracy across noise levels, but does not report training error on those runs. Its results address part of V4 using a test-performance measure, without testing the version's perfect-training-fit condition.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorizing data, but those cited results are not rows. It reports test accuracy under label noise in Tables 1 and A.1; it does not report training accuracy/error for these experiments. Its claims about regularizers and test performance do not establish whether they prevent fitting random labels.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization and regularizer performance under label noise, but never reports training fit to corrupted labels. Test accuracy alone cannot establish random-label memorization or V4's combination of perfect training fit and degrading generalization. The memorization finding is cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that the tested explicit regularizers share a tendency to increase model gradient similarity. They acknowledge that directly optimizing gradient-based penalties is computationally costly and requires more efficient computation or approximation for larger settings.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments compare regularization methods on motion-blurred MNIST with varying fractions of randomly flipped labels; they do not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiments or measure training fit.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with the fraction of randomly flipped labels, architecture, and regularization method; training-size and other parameter robustness are also examined.

fits_no_version.finding: Unregularized LeNet-5 final test accuracy falls from 89.6% to 62.0%, 37.3%, and 23.9% at 0%, 30%, 60%, and 80% label noise. Corresponding FCN accuracies are 82.1%, 59.5%, 36.9%, and 24.8%. No training accuracy is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On motion-blurred MNIST, unregularized networks generalize progressively worse as training-label noise increases over the reported levels.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and A.1 compare regularizers using test accuracy; Figures 2 and 3 associate better generalization with lower or more slowly growing MGS metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MGS regularization improves robustness to label noise in these benchmarks, and MGS metric trajectories track generalization performance.

record.problems: The label-noise experiments report test accuracy but not training accuracy/error, so they cannot establish whether networks fit corrupted or random training labels. The paper's comparisons are regularizer performance experiments, not direct tests of random-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the available label-noise results report test accuracy only and do not establish the training-fit behavior required by V4 or V5.

untested.parts: Training error on completely random labels, chance test performance on those runs, and fitting without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Whether networks maintain perfect training fit as label corruption increases and consequently memorize noise while capturing remaining signal. Test accuracy across noise levels is reported, but training fit is not.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing regularization preserves good generalization on true labels under otherwise matched training.
Direct measurement of learning real patterns before memorizing noisy labels. Test-accuracy peaks followed by declines do not separately measure those learning processes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 designation conflicts with its otherwise appropriate exclusion of test-performance results from memorization rows. Declining test accuracy does not establish training-label fitting; stable test accuracy under MGS does not establish that memorization was prevented. The omitted results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No training error or test error at chance is reported for completely randomized labels.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The study reports test accuracy as label-noise fraction changes, but does not report whether training fit remains perfect. No result rows are retained because the reported measure cannot establish the version's joint claim.
No random-label training-fit results with or without weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation.
No analysis of learning order or comparison of learning real-label patterns versus memorizing noise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
